newsitem.title: UK: Britain drafts business people into embassies.
newsitem.headline: Britain drafts business people into embassies.

text.p: Many of Britain's major companies have agreed to second staff to work in embassies abroad in an attempt to boost the country's export drive, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Wednesday.

He said the initiative is part of a scheme under which career diplomats will also spend periods working in industry to equip them for trade promotion activities when they return to the Foreign Office.

"I am delighted that we now have commitments from a number of leading companies to loan members of their staff to the FCO (Foreign and Commonwealth Office) to work on specific promotions or projects overseas for periods of a few months," Cook said in a parliamentary written answer.
The idea was welcomed by the Confederation of British Industry, whose president, Sir Colin Marshall, said: "I am delighted to support this imaginative scheme."
Companies participating in the scheme include British Airways, BOC, ICL, Wimpey, British Aerospace, British Telecommunications, HSBC and Glaxo Wellcome. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
